doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Session pay and the jazz guitarists playing rock and roll dates
summary: A three-hour session paid forty-one and a quarter, three sessions a day, with jazz guitarists like Mundell Lowe and Al Caiola playing three chords.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Wow. And what would a typical three hour session pay back then?
You’re going to laugh. Forty-one and a quarter.
Um hum. But you were doing three, sometimes four a day?
We did three, like three sessions a day.
And most of the guys were from the jazz and the swing—

Everybody was. Everybody was a jazz — I mean mostly all the guitar players, when we started doing those rock & roll dates, every one — Mundell Lowe, Billy Bauer, Chuck Wayne, Tony Mottola, Al Caiola — all great players, playing three chords.
